| **Summary** | No journal-specific AI-use policy page was found for Dialogue itself; the applicable rule is publisher-wide Cambridge University Press policy (announced 2023): generative AI/LLM tools may not be listed as an author; any use of generative AI in preparing a submission must be declared/explained (similar to disclosing other software/tools); authors remain fully accountable for accuracy, originality, and avoiding plagiarism. This is a disclosure-gated conditional-use policy, not an outright ban on AI assistance, but AI authorship is banned. **Current positioning (WO2, what the journal accepts now):** As of the 2026-07-13 check, the journal's own submission page states it has TEMPORARILY STOPPED ACCEPTING NEW ENGLISH SUBMISSIONS (backlog clearance) and is actively encouraging French submissions instead; authors already invited to revise a manuscript may still submit revisions via the 'Manuscripts with Decisions' portal. This is a critical, time-sensitive positioning fact for WO2.

**Methods noted as welcome (WO2, qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** analytic philosophy (traditional focus, per general reputation), philosophy engaging with Canadian political/social/cultural themes (per Vol. 65 Iss. 1 special issue 'Envisioning Canada': national identity, patriotism, Indigenous politics, language policy, philosophy of religion/pluralism, aesthetics/philosophy of music), critical notices and book symposia responding to recent monographs, bilingual/French-language philosophy papers (currently prioritized due to submission backlog)
